reflections.summary: Won through a well-suited Charizard Y/Raichu/Venusaur/Dragonite bring: Fake Out plus Heat Wave removed Whimsicott immediately, then Venusaur Sleep Powder and Raichu Encore/Electroweb neutralized Tauros and Sinistcha’s redirection, allowing Venusaur to clean. Mega Charizard Y was appropriate despite Tauros because Raichu and Venusaur controlled Tauros before it could threaten Charizard further.
reflections.adjustment: Keep this four and Mega Charizard Y plan, but continue prioritizing Tauros control/removal before leaving Charizard exposed to Rock Slide; if Tauros is on the field, use Raichu speed/control support or Venusaur Sleep Powder rather than freely attacking with Charizard.
reflections.notebook: Opponent showed a Whimsicott+Tauros opening, with Tauros willing to Protect on turn 1. Sinistcha’s main support pattern is repeated Rage Powder followed by Protect cycling; Raichu Encore can punish either option. reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the team-preview plan gave no immediate answer to Mega Charizard-Y sun: Whimsicott was exposed to Fake Out plus Heat Wave, Milotic could not establish Rain Dance before being removed by sun-boosted Solar Beam, and Tauros was then neutralized by Sleep Powder. With no Mega evolved, this four lacked enough pressure or weather control to break the Charizard/Venusaur/Raichu structure.
reflections.adjustment: Do not reuse this four unchanged. Bring an immediate anti-sun pairing that can withstand or bypass Fake Out and threaten Charizard/Venusaur, while preserving Rain Dance as a deliberate weather reversal rather than relying on Milotic to set it after taking damage. No suitable Mega Stone holder can be identified from the supplied evidence, so do not force a Mega choice without a confirmed anti-sun candidate.
